title: Resorbable magnesium metal membrane for sinus lift procedures: a case series
authors: Elad, A., Pul, L., Rider, P ., Rogge, S., Witte, F., Tadić, D., Mijiritsky, E., Kačarević, Ž. P ., & Steigmann, L. (2023). BMC oral health, 23(1), 1006.
supports: Clinical study from the botiss maxgraft granules (processed human allograft) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “Within the limitations of this case series, postoperative clinical examinati on, and panoramic and CBCT images demonstrated that resorbable magnesium membrane is a viable material for sinus lift and Schneiderian membrane repair. The case series showed successful healing and formation of new alveolar bone with separation of the oral cavity and maxillary sinus in four patients” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
